Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1. Heard Mr. Gaurav Sharma, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Arjun Singh Yadav, the learned counsel
for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Perused the record.

3. This application for bail has been filed by applicant-Rinku Rajput, seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 260 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 504, 506 IPC, Sections 3/4 POCSO Act and Sections 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, Police Station-Saini, District-Kaushambi during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Rinku Rajput vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. contends that notice of present application for bail has been served upon first informant-opposite party 4 on 22.08.2023.

However, in spite of service of notice,
no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant-opposite party 4 to oppose this application for bail.

5. Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred in between 12.06.2023 to 19.06.2023, a delayed FIR dated 23.06.2023 was lodged by first informant-Jai Prakash Raidas (Father of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 260 of 2023, under Sections 366, 376, 504, 506 IPC and Sections 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, Police Station-Saini,
District-Kaushambi.
In the aforesaid FIR, one person namely Rinku (applicant herein) has been nominated as named accused whereas 2 other persons have also been arraigned as accused.
6. The gravamen of the allegations made in the FIR is to the effect that daughter of first informant i.e. the prosecutrix namely X went missing on 12.06.2023.
Accordingly, a missing person report was lodged.
Subsequently, the daughter of first informant returned on 19.06.2023.
While the prosecutrix had gone to attend the call of nature, 2 persons are alleged to have come on a motorcycle and thereafter, forcibly abducted the prosecutrix.
The FIR further records that named accused deliberately dislodged the modesty of the prosecutrix.
7. After above-mentioned FIR was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter-XII Cr.P.C.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Same is on record at page 25 of the paper book.
The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has supported the FIR but has also stated that she accompanied the applicant to Allahabad and thereafter went to Bombay with the applicant.

She has,
however, stated that her modesty was deliberately dislodged by the applicant.

Subsequent to above,
the prosecutrix was requested for her medico legal examination.
The prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor, who medically examined her, has rejoined her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
However, the Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix, did not find any such signs on her person so as to denote commission of deliberate or forceful sexual assault.

With regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, the Doctor has opined as follows;-
"Hymen Perineum - Torned & Healed"
8.
Certain samples were collected from the body of prosecutrix for pathological examination.
However, the results of the same are in negative.
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

Same is on record at page 52 of the paper book wherein, she has reiterated her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
9.
Investigating Officer further examined first informant and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Witnesses so examined have substantially supported the FIR.
Since the prosecutrix is an illiterate lady, therefore, there is no educational record qua the date of birth of the prosecutrix.
Accordingly, the medical determination of age of the prosecutrix was conducted.
Same is on record at page 43 of the paper book.
As per the medical opinion, the prosecutrix is said to be aged about 15 to17 years.

On the basis of above and other material collected by the Investigating Officer during Rinku Rajput vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50685826/
2 course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that complicity of applicant is fully established in the crime in question.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He, accordingly, submitted the charge sheet dated 08.07.2023 against appliant only whereby applicant has been charge sheeted under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 504, 506 IPC, Sections 3/4 POCSO Act and Sections 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act.
10. Learned counsel for applicant contends that though applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
Referring to the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., he submits that initially the prosecutrix joined the applicant readily and willingly.
She, thereafter, accompanied the applicant to Allahabad and then to Bombay.
The prosecutrix stayed with the applicant for a sufficiently long time.
However, no objection was raised by the prosecutrix.
As such, the prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party.

Attention of the Court was then invited to the Medico Legal Examination Report of the prosecutrix and on basis thereof, it is urged that the Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix, did not find any such signs on her body so as to denote commission of deliberate or forceful sexual assault.
As such, no offence under Section 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act can be said to have been committed by the applicant.
As such, applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
11. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as, he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 24.06.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than 5 and 1/2 months of incarceration.

The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
has already been submitted.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged on record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
On the above premise, he submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that since applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The prosecutrix is a young girl aged about 15 to 17 years as per the medical opinion.
The applicant is guilty of dislodging the modesty of the prosecutrix, who is an unmarried young girl.
As such, no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicant.

However, the learned A.G.A. could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of the present application for bail with reference to the record at this stage.

13. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, accusations made, complicity of accused and coupled with the fact that the prosecutrix herself joined the applicant and thereafter, accompanied him to Allahabad and thereafter to Bombay, the prosecutrix stayed with the applicant for a sufficiently long time, as such, the prosecutrix was neither abducted, kidnapped or enticed away by the applicant, as such prima-facie no offence under Sections 363, 366 IPC can be said to have been committed by applicant, however, no objection was raised by the prosecutrix, as such, the prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party, the Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix,
did not find any such signs on her body so as to denote commission of deliberate or forceful sexual assault, as such, no offence under Section 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act can be said to have Rinku Rajput vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50685826/
3 been committed by the applicant, the clean antecedents of applicant, the period of incarceration undergone, the police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted,
therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized, yet in spite of above, the learned A.G.A. could not point out any such circumstance from the record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, therefore,
irrespective of the objections raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to the present application for bail, but without making any comments on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.
14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant-Rinku Rajput, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.
IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.

(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSES THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.
(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C.

IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.

Rinku Rajput vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50685826/
4

entities.text: Rinku Rajput vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.

16. However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his bail so granted by this Court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
